topic: Sharp aggregate-ATT regions under latent-transition type mergers. In the compact binary four-period at-most-two-type Ahn–Kasahara model, with the pre-treatment transition shared across treatment arms within type and all primitive probabilities in [η,1−η] for fixed rational 0<η<0.15, define the global transition-alignment fiber of the full observed path PMF. Prove a branch-complete 16-chart full-path factorization covering terminal collisions, rank failures, all probability-box faces, and every cross-arm alignment; derive explicit observable vanishing/sign conditions necessary and sufficient for aggregate ATT at dates 3 and 4 to be point identified; otherwise compute the attained sharp region, allowing disconnected finite unions of intervals, by a terminating branch-aware exact algorithm. Give uniformly honest confidence regions for the entire identified set and endpoint/Hausdorff consistency under explicit branch-continuity conditions. Consumer: the public ak package and its Dodd–Frank, Norwegian patenting, and ADA analyses, whose reported ATT sign and bootstrap uncertainty change at merger fibers. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Full path tensors, not pair moments, are necessary. Sixteen terminal-collision charts yield explicit splitting formulas, eight rank-one constraints, and four cross-arm alignment equations. A positive law has exactly two attainable ATT values. For the supplied merger law, every unequal-ATT representation has common prehistory and falls into four control cases; convexity fixes extremizing arm weights, reducing full endpoints to four eight-inequality polygon problems. At η=1/10, exact rational arithmetic gives I3=[−8867/29480,7517/29480] and I4=[−8611/29480,7773/29480], both crossing zero; endpoint PMFs and an η=7/50 branch switch were checked. Pair-moment insufficiency, terminal collisions, coincident components, disconnected regions, and fixed-coverage Hausdorff failure were tested; no exact literature collision was found. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Derive model-specific observable vanishing/sign tests that are necessary and sufficient for all sixteen feasible chart images to coincide at one ATT value, including rank deficiencies, alignments, and box contacts, without substituting unrestricted multivariate quantifier elimination. EARLY KILL TEST: Independently verify the sixteen-chart reconstruction, then completely classify the case with distinct treated terminal rows and exactly one collided control terminal row. An omitted legal branch or classification requiring only unrestricted generic QE triggers a pivot before expanding the atlas. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/pid_transition_merge_att_region.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Give observable necessary-and-sufficient conditions for aggregate ATT at dates 3 and 4 to be constant on the full transition-alignment fiber of the binary four-period, at-most-two-type Ahn–Kasahara model, including every terminal collision, rank loss, cross-arm alignment, and η-box contact.

source_refs.claim: Their point-identification proof assumes nonsingular reconstruction matrices and distinct eigenvalues, and their asymptotic theory additionally assumes nonsingular Fisher information; it does not classify the fibers where these conditions fail.
source_refs.author: Young Ahn and Hiroyuki Kasahara

source_refs.claim: Kruskal-based arguments establish generic identifiability of latent-structure models while explicitly leaving a measure-zero nonidentified exceptional set unclassified.
source_refs.author: Elizabeth S. Allman, Catherine Matias, and John A. Rhodes

source_refs.claim: For binary HMMs, polynomial invariants, a birational inverse, and a semialgebraic membership test replace a merely generic reconstruction, but no treatment-arm alignment or causal ATT functional is analyzed.
source_refs.author: Andrew J. Critch

open_problems.why_unsolved: Ahn–Kasahara’s reconstruction diagonalizes observable matrix products only after imposing latent-parameter nonsingularity and distinct-eigenvalue conditions; at component mergers, eigenvectors cease to label types and treated and control decompositions can admit multiple cross-arm matchings. Generic latent-class results certify identification off an algebraic exceptional set but do not determine whether aggregate ATT remains invariant on that exceptional fiber. Critch’s semialgebraic HMM analysis suggests how to describe exceptional strata, yet its single-process parameterization has neither two treatment arms sharing pre-treatment transitions nor an ATT functional. The literature scan found no branch-complete observable criterion for constancy of this causal functional.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite semialgebraic list of observable vanishing and sign conditions, proved equivalent to constancy of both ATT coordinates on every feasible chart of the global fiber, together with explicit counter-witnesses whenever any condition fails.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its progression from failures of discrete-outcome DiD to transition independence, latent transition heterogeneity, and empirically consequential ATT recovery, then locate the new question at its identification boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Discrete outcomes make parallel trends problematic -> transition independence supplies a dynamic counterfactual -> latent Markov types address unobserved transition heterogeneity -> component mergers defeat regular identification and require an observable ATT-fiber criterion

method_exemplars.technique: Use observable polynomial invariants, a rational inverse on regular charts, and semialgebraic membership inequalities; adapt the proof by intersecting two arm-specific decompositions through their shared pre-treatment transition parameters.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It demonstrates how to pass from generic tensor recovery to explicit observable tests and fiber analysis in a four-node binary latent Markov model.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the three-block tensor/Kruskal decomposition proof, replacing its generic rank conclusion with a direct classification of the rank-deficient two-component boundary.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Ahn–Kasahara’s regular reconstruction and the proposed collision atlas share the same latent-class tensor-factorization structure.

method_exemplars.technique: Retain their full-path likelihood and influence-function ATT estimator on regular charts while making explicit where the distinct-eigenvalue and nonsingular-information proof steps cease to apply.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It estimates the identical aggregate causal estimand in the identical short-panel model and supplies the regular branch that a complete theory must recover.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a terminating exact algorithm that returns the attained sharp joint region for (ATT3, ATT4) over the full feasible transition-alignment fiber as a finite union of semialgebraic arcs or interval components with endpoint witnesses, rather than only numerical outer bounds.

source_refs.claim: The paper reports point-identified latent-type and aggregate ATTs under Assumption ID and estimates them by full-path finite-mixture likelihood, but does not define or compute the ATT image when Assumption ID fails.
source_refs.author: Young Ahn and Hiroyuki Kasahara

source_refs.claim: They exactly characterize partially identified finite mixtures under an excluded source of mixture-weight variation, including discrete outcomes, but not arm-aligned Markov mixtures or ATT images.
source_refs.author: Marc Henry, Yuichi Kitamura, and Bernard Salanié

source_refs.claim: Discrete causal bounds are reduced to polynomial programs and approximated by spatial branch-and-bound with ε-sharp certificates; analytic nonlinear bounds remain case-specific.
source_refs.author: Guilherme Duarte, Noam Finkelstein, Dean Knox, Jonathan Mummolo, and Ilya Shpitser
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: Ahn–Kasahara stops at a regular point-identification regime. Henry–Kitamura–Salanié gives exact mixture identified sets when an exclusion moves weights without moving components, whereas the destination model couples two arm-specific path tensors through shared latent pre-treatment transitions and admits finite label alignments and collision strata. Autobounds supplies a general numerical polynomial-program route with asymptotic ε-sharpness, but it neither exploits this low-dimensional chart structure nor returns a symbolic, attained, disconnected image with exact endpoint representations. The first proof step that must change is the replacement of a single convex or connected feasible parameter set by enumeration and exact projection of all alignment-and-collision charts.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite branch-aware exact-arithmetic algorithm with a termination proof that outputs the complete attained ATT image, decomposes it into connected components, and supplies a feasible latent representation for every reported endpoint plus an infeasibility certificate for every discarded branch.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its shift from failed point identification to an exact characterization of all observationally compatible mixtures and their testable restrictions.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Finite mixtures encode economically important latent heterogeneity -> common point-identification conditions can fail -> observational equivalence should be characterized rather than ignored -> project the exact arm-aligned Markov mixture fiber onto aggregate ATT

method_exemplars.technique: Translate observational compatibility and the causal target into polynomial constraints, use feasible primal witnesses and certified branch bounds, then replace asymptotic spatial refinement with exact low-dimensional chart elimination.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It treats sharp causal bounds as optimization over observationally indistinguishable discrete data-generating processes, exactly the fiber-image interpretation needed here.

method_exemplars.technique: Use birational chart inverses and semialgebraic membership conditions to isolate exceptional components before projecting the causal functional.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its four-node binary latent Markov geometry is structurally closest to the path-PMF charts, although the new proof must add treatment-arm coupling.

method_exemplars.technique: Profile a likelihood or minimum-distance criterion over the exact feasible fiber and invert quasi-likelihood-ratio level sets; adapt their arguments for partially identified models and singular points.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The sharp region is an image of minimizers of a nonlinear criterion and may move between point and partial identification.

open_problems.open_problem: Develop confidence regions that uniformly cover the entire possibly disconnected aggregate-ATT identified set across regular, collision, rank-deficient, alignment-switching, and η-box-contact sequences, while also establishing endpoint and Hausdorff consistency on explicitly characterized branch-continuity strata.

source_refs.claim: Its weighted bootstrap and simultaneous ATT bands are derived after assuming interior primitive probabilities and nonsingular Fisher information, so merger fibers and changing identified-set topology are outside the stated asymptotic result.
source_refs.author: Young Ahn and Hiroyuki Kasahara

source_refs.claim: Monte Carlo criterion-based confidence sets are uniformly valid over point- and partially identified models and exact for subvectors at some singularities, but can be conservative on boundary-cone cases.
source_refs.author: Xiaohong Chen, Timothy M. Christensen, and Elie Tamer

source_refs.claim: For Gaussian first-stage limits, the ordinary bootstrap is consistent for a transformed parameter only under full differentiability; modified resampling is needed for directionally differentiable maps.
source_refs.author: Zheng Fang and Andres Santos

source_refs.claim: They construct random sets with pointwise and, under additional conditions, uniform coverage of general criterion-defined identified sets and their images.
source_refs.author: Joseph P. Romano and Azeem M. Shaikh

open_problems.why_unsolved: At a merger, the parameter-to-path-law map loses rank, labels or alignments switch, and the ATT image can gain, lose, or separate connected components. The ordinary weighted bootstrap used for the regular Ahn–Kasahara estimator is therefore not licensed: Fang–Santos identifies nondifferentiability as the condition under which the standard bootstrap generally fails. General set-inference procedures cover criterion minimizers and some singularities, but they do not by themselves give model-specific endpoint or Hausdorff consistency when the target is the image of a changing union of algebraic branches. Uniform coverage and Hausdorff consistency must be separated because the latter can fail without local branch persistence or a gap condition between feasible and infeasible charts.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A computable confidence-region procedure with a theorem proving uniform whole-set coverage over a stated neighborhood of merger laws, plus endpoint and Hausdorff convergence rates under explicit branch-persistence, transversality, and component-separation conditions and counterexamples when those conditions fail.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its identification-robust framing: researchers often cannot know whether a nonlinear model is point identified, so inference should remain valid over both point- and set-identified sequences.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Nonlinear models can move between point and partial identification -> regular asymptotics are unreliable near singularities -> criterion inversion can cover the whole identified set -> specialize it to branch-changing ATT fibers and add Hausdorff guarantees

method_exemplars.technique: Construct profile-criterion level sets and simulate quasi-posterior QLR cutoffs; adapt the local tangent-cone and singular-subvector arguments to the finite union of model-specific charts.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly targets uniform coverage across point and partial identification in nonlinear latent-variable models.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive the directional derivative of each branch endpoint or value map and use derivative-aware resampling instead of the naive bootstrap at maximum, minimum, and branch-switch points.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Sharp endpoints formed by minima and maxima over competing charts are directionally but generally not fully differentiable.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert tests of a population criterion and use subsampling-style uniformity arguments to obtain random sets covering the full minimizer set or its ATT image.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired inferential object is the entire image of a criterion-defined identified set, not merely one selected endpoint.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the minimal collection of observed path marginals that preserves the aggregate-ATT fiber in the binary four-period Ahn–Kasahara model, proving when pair-transition moments are insufficient and when specified triple or full-path cells are sufficient after cross-arm alignment.

source_refs.claim: Its posterior classification and finite-mixture likelihood use each unit’s full observation vector, while its identification proof forms matrix products from several full-path probabilities; minimal observable information is not characterized.
source_refs.author: Young Ahn and Hiroyuki Kasahara

source_refs.claim: Under a weak nondegeneracy condition, length-three trails uniquely reconstruct mixtures of Markov chains; identical component chains remain observationally inseparable regardless of trail length.
source_refs.author: Rishi Gupta, Ravi Kumar, and Sergei Vassilvitskii
source_refs.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 29

source_refs.claim: Three conditionally independent observed blocks form a tensor whose Kruskal ranks can identify latent components, highlighting information present in joint triples but absent from pairwise matrix factorizations.
source_refs.author: Elizabeth S. Allman, Catherine Matias, and John A. Rhodes

open_problems.why_unsolved: Three-way tensors can break the rotational ambiguity of two-way factorizations, and length-three trails reconstruct ordinary Markov-chain mixtures away from degeneracy. The Ahn–Kasahara target, however, is not recovery of one mixture: treatment and control decompositions must be aligned through common pre-treatment dynamics, and aggregate ATT may be identified even if latent parameters are not. The first proof step must therefore change from component reconstruction to comparison of ATT fibers induced by competing marginalization operators. The literature scan found no result characterizing which pairs, triples, or four-way cells preserve this causal functional in the arm-aligned latent-transition model.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessity-and-sufficiency theorem for ATT preservation under explicit marginalization maps, including observationally equivalent full-path laws with identical pair moments but different ATT as necessity witnesses and a constructive reconstruction-and-alignment formula for every sufficient marginal collection.

writing_exemplar.why: Use its short-panel motivation and full-path latent-type construction, then sharpen the empirical question from whether the model is identified to exactly which path information is indispensable.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Short panels must reveal latent transition heterogeneity -> full trajectory likelihood contains higher-order dependence -> commonly used pair transitions discard that dependence -> characterize the minimal observed marginals that still determine aggregate ATT

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the length-three-trail matrix decomposition and its nondegeneracy proof, then impose common-prehistory matching across the two treatment arms.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It gives an explicit minimal-short-trajectory reconstruction result for mixtures of Markov chains rather than a generic latent-class theorem.

method_exemplars.technique: Use Kruskal’s three-block uniqueness argument to prove triple sufficiency and explicit rank-two matrix symmetries to construct pairwise-moment counterexamples.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The contrast between pair matrices and three-way tensors is the structural source of the proposed minimal-information result.

method_exemplars.technique: Compare the paper’s full-path MLE and influence-function estimator with GMM estimators based only on candidate sufficient marginal cells, carrying through an asymptotic variance and efficiency comparison.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the target-specific regular estimator against which information-reduced estimators must be judged.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the η-sensitivity phase diagram of the sharp aggregate-ATT region, identifying all critical η values at which a probability-box face enters an extremizer or the number, ordering, or connectivity of attainable ATT components changes.

source_refs.claim: Their finite-mixture identified set is defined by exact linear and quadratic probability constraints, but they do not analyze topology changes induced by a common lower and upper probability bound.
source_refs.author: Marc Henry, Yuichi Kitamura, and Bernard Salanié

source_refs.claim: The binary-HMM observable model is represented semialgebraically with rational inverse charts, machinery suited to parameter-dependent feasibility but not applied to probability-box sensitivity of causal fibers.
source_refs.author: Andrew J. Critch

source_refs.claim: Their framework supports sensitivity analysis by changing domain assumptions and recomputing polynomial bounds, but provides numerical ε-sharp bounds rather than a symbolic phase diagram in the sensitivity parameter.
source_refs.author: Guilherme Duarte, Noam Finkelstein, Dean Knox, Jonathan Mummolo, and Ilya Shpitser
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: A common η-bound changes the feasible latent-transition fiber itself rather than merely truncating a fixed ATT interval. Active faces can switch between charts, and distinct attainable components can merge or disappear, so ordinary endpoint comparative statics on one smooth optimizer are inadequate. Existing exact finite-mixture characterizations do not include this shared transition-alignment geometry, while general polynomial-bounding software reruns numerical optimization at selected η values and does not certify the complete list of breakpoints. The first new proof step is parametric semialgebraic projection of each collision-and-alignment chart followed by a proof that the resulting critical-value list is exhaustive. The scan found no Ahn–Kasahara-specific η phase diagram.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite partition of the rational η-domain into cells on which the number of ATT components and every endpoint’s algebraic formula are fixed, with exact critical η values, extremizing latent representations, and one-sided Hausdorff limits at every branch switch.

writing_exemplar.why: Adopt its emphasis on how explicit probability restrictions convert observational equivalence into an interpretable identified set, then treat η as a transparent restriction-strength index.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Finite-mixture observables permit many latent decompositions -> probability restrictions shrink the compatible family -> applied conclusions depend on restriction strength -> derive the exact η values at which the sharp ATT region changes topology or formula

method_exemplars.technique: Combine rational inverse charts with semialgebraic membership inequalities and eliminate chart parameters while retaining η as a free coordinate.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A parametric semialgebraic description is the natural vehicle for an exhaustive finite-breakpoint theorem.

method_exemplars.technique: Use polynomialized targets and branch-feasibility certificates to validate extrema on each η-cell, replacing numerical subdivision with exact root isolation in the low-dimensional specialized model.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the closest general method for sensitivity analysis of sharp discrete causal bounds under changing domain restrictions.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt random-set consistency and Hausdorff-metric arguments cell by cell, treating critical η values separately where support-function regularity or component separation fails.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The phase diagram is empirically useful only if its estimated set converges in a set metric as the probability restrictions and observed PMF vary.

literature_map:
Ahn–Kasahara (2026, arXiv:2603.07914) is the exact destination anchor: short-panel discrete ATT under transition independence with latent-type Markov dynamics, full-path likelihood, and three policy applications.
Its identification proof uses nonsingular observable-factor matrices, distinct eigenvalues, and cross-state permutation alignment; its inference assumes interior probabilities and nonsingular Fisher information.
Allman–Matias–Rhodes (2009, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:0809.5032) supplies the foundational Kruskal/tensor route to generic latent-class and HMM identifiability but leaves exceptional fibers unclassified.
Critch (2013, Journal of Algebraic Statistics, arXiv:1206.0500) gives a birational inverse, polynomial invariants, and semialgebraic membership tests for four-node binary HMMs, the closest algebraic-geometry analogue.
Gupta–Kumar–Vassilvitskii (2016, NeurIPS) reconstructs mixtures of Markov chains from length-three trails under nondegeneracy and notes that coincident chains cannot be separated.
Hsu–Kakade–Zhang (2012, JCSS, arXiv:0811.4413) and Anandkumar–Hsu–Kakade (2012, COLT) show how observable low-order moments support spectral learning under rank and separation conditions.
Henry–Kitamura–Salanié (2014, Quantitative Economics, DOI 10.3982/QE170) exactly partially identifies finite mixtures with weight-shifting exclusions, including discrete outcomes, but not coupled treatment-arm Markov mixtures.
Kitamura–Laage (arXiv:1811.02727) gives alternative nonparametric finite-mixture identification strategies and polynomial-rate estimation, again away from the destination’s merger geometry.
Duarte–Finkelstein–Knox–Mummolo–Shpitser (2024, JASA, arXiv:2109.13471) reduces sharp discrete causal bounds to polynomial programming with spatial branch-and-bound and ε-sharp certificates.
Beresteanu–Molinari (2008, Econometrica) establishes random-set and Hausdorff asymptotics for a class of partially identified models, primarily through convex-set machinery.
Romano–Shaikh (2010, Econometrica) gives general criterion-based confidence regions with uniform identified-set coverage under stated conditions.
Chen–Christensen–Tamer (2018, Econometrica, arXiv:1605.00499) gives identification-robust Monte Carlo confidence sets across point, partial, boundary-cone, and some singular cases.
Fang–Santos (2019, Review of Economic Studies, arXiv:1404.3763) explains failure of the ordinary bootstrap for merely directionally differentiable endpoint and selection maps and supplies derivative-aware resampling.
Cho–Russell (arXiv:1810.03180) and Gafarov (2025, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:1904.00111) obtain uniform endpoint inference for linear or affine polygonal sets, but their convex affine geometry excludes nonlinear disconnected chart unions.
The live tension is that the destination paper supplies regular point identification and bootstrap inference, while adjacent algebraic, partial-identification, and inference literatures provide transferable machinery but no branch-complete ATT-fiber classification, exact disconnected-region algorithm, or merger-uniform set inference for this model.
